title: Lockup
logline: Branch A, the first hour after the vote: Nandini arrests Nirala by the book, locks him in her own thana's cobwebbed lockup, and at ten past twelve lets eight hundred sacks leave town on her own SHO's stamp. From behind the bars her prisoner tells her how to fight back, and the first door she knocks on shuts in her face.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; 'madam', 'thana', 'FIR', 'SHO sahab', 'ji', 'almirah' and 'lakh'-style Indian terms kept as spoken in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana, six weeks into her first posting. Tonight she chose the book.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip (empty in this episode: the cuffs are on Nirala); black shoes; blue ballpoint pen in her left chest pocket. No cap, no stars. Cherry-red open-face helmet: on the lobby bench in b1 and b2, under her left arm from b3 (set down on the SHO's desk in b4, picked up in b5, in her left hand in b6 and b7; set down by the doorway in b8 and never in frame again); no helmet in frame from b8 on (D-016 direction 19).
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent: not British, not American. Says 'madam', 'thana', 'FIR', 'ji' and 'SHO sahab' as Indian officers do. Quick and clipped by habit; in this episode she is under pressure the whole time, so she is quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. Her lines at the crossing (l08 to l11) are said like entries in a diary, not like a lament.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The man who ran the fake thana. Under arrest from the first second, in his own uniform.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping, sleeves to the knuckles, collar standing off the neck, belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. The only peaked cap in the series (khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge), dead level, never taken off. Big blank brass-yellow medal on a maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon above his left chest pocket. Empty brown leather holster on his right hip from b2 on. Plain steel handcuffs on BOTH wrists from b1 to the end of the episode.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned small-town north-Indian English, as learnt from manuals ('kindly', 'the same'), with a clear Hindi accent: not British, not American. Every English police word said with great care; no contractions. Courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Frightened tonight: a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. When he gets the idea in b9 he is still quiet but firmer, a clerk who knows the procedure.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Has kept the second almirah key for two years.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with two steel knitting needles crossed through it. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on teal epaulettes, lantern patches, khaki trousers, black shoes. Over it a hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan, open, two sagging pockets; a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town Indian English with a clear Hindi accent, short sentences: not British, not American. Never surprised; warmth shows only as dryness. Her two jokes in this episode (l06, l24) are said completely straight.

characters.name: Ramsevak
characters.role: The first complainant from the red file. One shot, one line, never recurs as a face.
characters.look: Thin man, 50s, grey stubble, white vest, a shawl pulled round him, seen through a wooden door open a hand's width at 1 a.m.
characters.voice_note: Tired, flat, older male. Small-town Indian English with a strong Hindi accent: not British, not American. One line, not hostile: a man who has finished with hoping. Fully voiced, not whispered; it is the episode's last line.

location: Four of the seven series plates: talkies_lobby (b1, b2), crossing_stall (b3, b6, b7), real_thana (b4, b5, b8, b9, b10), lane_doorway (b11). Fictional town of Imlipur, a railway line cutting it in two. All night, no crowd.
time_of_day: Night: 11 p.m. in b1, midnight in b5, ten past twelve in b7, 1 a.m. in b11. Clocks are painted with hands and no numerals; every time that matters is spoken.

beats.action: OPENS ON A SOUND: the ratchet of handcuffs, on frame one. Talkies lobby, night, one bare bulb over the old booking counter. Shot 1 (close, the hook): Nirala's two wrists held out across the desk, sleeves over his knuckles, and Nandini's hands closing the steel on them; the ratchet and 'Sudhir Nirala.' play over it. Shot 2 (Nandini single, profile, eyes on the cuffs): the rest of l01. Shot 3 (two-shot, Nandini picture-left in profile, Nirala picture-right): he bows his head once, cap dead level; l02 and l03 play over it. Pushpa is in the room but out of frame (two sheet faces per frame at most, D-016 direction 14).

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Sudhir Nirala. For posing as a police officer and running a thana, you are under arrest.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Yes, madam.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [hesitant] Only... kindly let the cap stay.

beats.action: Same lobby. Shot 1 (insert): the wooden revolver lying in profile on the desk goes into a small cloth bag; his cuffed hands drip a blob of his own red wax on the knot (a stick of red sealing wax and a matchbox from his desk drawer); l04 plays over it. Shot 2 (two-shot, Nirala and Nandini): he dictates, she writes the blank tag with her blue pen; l05 plays over it. Shot 3 (wide, after the lines): Pushpa, the red-cloth file under her arm and the sealed bag in her hand, reaches up to the bulb; the click is heard and the lobby goes dark behind three figures (Pushpa as a silhouette).

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] 'One revolver, wooden. Recovered from the accused.'

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Kindly put the date, madam.

beats.action: One wide still, no dialogue. The railway crossing at night: the signal lamp, the single track across frame, three silhouettes stepping over the rails: a tall straight one with a round helmet under one arm, a short square one with needles crossed in her bun, and between them a small one under a level peaked cap, wrists together in front of him. He crosses the line to the real thana for the first time.

The real thana at night, one tube light. Shot 1: at the back, the cobwebbed barred door of the lockup; Pushpa's hands fight a rusted padlock, a cobweb across the bars, Nandini behind her as a back, setting her red helmet down on the SHO's desk; l06 plays over it. Shot 2 (inside the cell, after the line): Nirala steps in, dusts the bench with his handkerchief and sits bolt upright, cap level, medal on, cuffed hands on his knees. Shot 3 (GLIMPSE A IMAGE): the barred door closes on a small man in full uniform; the clang is the cut.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] First prisoner in two years. Even the lock had forgotten how to open.

beats.action: Shot 1 (insert): the wall clock, hands meeting at twelve. Shot 2 (through the bars, Nirala picture-right in the cell, Nandini picture-left outside): he looks at the clock and says where he should be; l07 plays over it. After the line she picks up her red helmet from the SHO's desk and goes out of the doorway without answering (one frame of the empty doorway).

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Twelve o'clock. Bhaiyaji will be waiting.

beats.action: The crossing, a few minutes past twelve. Shot 1 (wide): the red-and-white gate arm down; behind it the truck (dull orange cab, high load under a grey tarpaulin, blank number plate) with its headlights on; Nandini steps into the headlights, helmet in her left hand, right hand raised; l08 plays over it (GLIMPSE A ENDS on l08; nothing after it is in the glimpse). Shot 2 (insert): a forearm out of the cab window and the pink slip (painted blank; overlay ov_slip_signature) now in her hand in the headlights; l09 plays over it. Shot 3 (close, her face lit from below by the headlights, the slip in front of her): l10 plays over it.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Stop. Show me the papers.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Eight hundred sacks. Signed by... SHO Tripathi. With his stamp.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] The papers are in order.

beats.action: Not in Glimpse A. Shot 1 (insert, during the silence): her hand gives the slip back up to the forearm; the gate arm stands raised (one frame, the creak and the gear engaging are sound). Shot 2 (held image): red tail-lights going away over the railway line into the dark, Nandini's back to camera, helmet hanging in her hand; l11 plays over it, said like an entry.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Ten past twelve. Eight hundred sacks. I let them go.

beats.action: STATE: helmet set down by the doorway, out of frame. No helmet in frame from here to the end of the episode. Back at the bars, tube light. Shot 1 (Nirala single, at the bars, cuffed hands on a bar): l12. Shot 2 (Nandini single, outside the bars): l13. Shot 3 (Nirala single): he turns the fact over like a clerk, l14 and l15. Shot 4 (Nandini single): she finishes the thought, l16. Shot 5 (insert, the silence after): his cuffed hand goes to his collar.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] The truck has gone, madam?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Gone. At ten past twelve. On SHO sahab's signature.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] It was already stamped by SHO sahab, madam?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Then my stamp was not needed at all.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] So the invitation was never for the stamp. It was for you.

beats.action: Not in Glimpse A. Shot 1 (Nirala single): he gets up off the bench and comes to the bars, cap level; l17 plays over it. Shot 2 (insert): his cuffed hands round a bar; l18 plays over it. Shot 3 (Nandini single, the SHO's desk and the red file on it behind her): she takes the clock as her own fact; l19 plays over it. Shot 4 (insert): her hand coming down flat on the red file on the SHO's desk; l20 plays over it. Shot 5 (through the bars, two-shot of Nirala and Nandini; in the picture-left foreground Pushpa's knitting hands, stopped, needles still): l21 and l22.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] The sacks have gone, madam. The complaints have not.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] But my files are fake-thana papers. Kindly enter the same in the real register.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] At ten this morning there will be microphones in this thana.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Nobody can bury a register kept in front of them.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [hesitant] After that... SHO sahab's almirah.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Write the FIR, madam.

beats.action: Shot 1 (two-shot, Nandini and Pushpa at the tall grey steel almirah): Nandini looks at the padlock; Pushpa draws a loop of orange wool out of her cardigan pocket with a small steel key on it, held up between them; l23 plays over it. Shot 2 (wide on the almirah): the door open, the big green cloth-bound register coming out in a puff of dust in Pushpa's hands; l24 plays over it. Shot 3 (high angle over Nandini's shoulder): the register open on the SHO's desk in the foreground, blank ruled pages, her hand flat on them; beyond the desk, on the wall, the zero-crime shield (overlay ov_shield); l25 plays over it. In the silence after, two knocks on wood are heard as a pre-lap into b11.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] The second key, madam.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Two years I've been waiting for someone to ask.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] So this is zero crime.

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN. Not in Glimpse A. One a.m., the lane: one narrow brick lane, one wooden double door with a stone step and an iron chain latch, the wall lamp lit, 1 a.m. blue light; a bicycle leaning by the step. Shot 1 (Nandini single, from the side): the red file under her left arm, the green register held flat against her chest by the same arm, her right hand's knuckles just off the wood after knocking; the door is open a hand's width on its chain; l26 plays over it. Shot 2 (single, through the gap, the episode's one minor face): Ramsevak, shawl round him, looking at the two bars on her shoulder, not at her face; l27 plays over it. Shot 3 (held, after the line): the shut door, and her right hand still half raised in front of it.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Ramsevak ji. I've come to write your FIR. Against Bhaiyaji.

lines.speaker: door1_man
lines.text: [sighs] We went to the real thana once, madam.

sfx_notes: Bed, b1 and b2: the shut talkies at night, a big empty room: faint ceiling creak, one moth ticking against the bare bulb, crickets outside the high windows.
b1: handcuff ratchet on frame one, close and dry, two clicks (one per wrist). Nothing else under it for the first second.
b2: cloth bag drawstring; a match strike and the soft drip of wax; pen scratch on the tag under l05; after the lines, a bulb switch click and the room tone drops as the light goes.
b3: footsteps on railway ballast (three rhythms: long even strides, short brisk steps, small careful steps with a faint clink of steel cuffs); the signal relay ticking; crickets. No train.
Bed, b4, b5, b8 to b10: the real thana at night: tube-light hum, slow ceiling fan, a far dog once in b8.
b4: a rusted padlock grinding and refusing under l06, then giving; the barred door swinging shut, one heavy iron clang that ends the beat. Keep the clang clear of l06.
b5: the wall clock tick, one tick louder as the hands meet; footsteps leaving; the helmet lifted off the desk.

b6: diesel truck idling, close and low, with headlight glare as a faint electrical hum. Duck the engine right down under l08 ('Stop. Show me the papers.'): it is Glimpse A's last line and must be fully intelligible. Paper rustle as the slip changes hands; keep the idle low under l09 and l10.

b7: the gate arm creaking up; the truck going into gear and pulling away over the rails (wheels thudding the track twice), the engine fading into the distance under l11, which sits on the fade, not on the gear change. Then crickets.
b8: tube-light hum; a soft brush of cloth as his hand goes to his collar.

b9: the bench creaks as he stands; cuff chain against an iron bar once, on the cut to shot 2 between l17 and l18, not under either line. Pushpa's needles click under l17 and l18 and stop dead before l19.

b10: padlock click, almirah door groaning open, a dull thump and a breath of dust as the register comes out; one page turn under l25. Two knocks on wood in the silence after l25, as a pre-lap into b11.

b11: night lane: a far dog, a moth at the wall lamp. The chain latch rattles taut as the door stops a hand's width open, before l26. After l27 has finished, the door shuts and the bolt is shot: solid, close, then near silence for the hold. Nothing loud sits on l27; the bed is down to almost nothing under it.
music_note: No music from b1 to b6: the arrest and the lockup are played on room sound. One low, sustained string note enters under the tail-lights in b7 and holds through l11; it is gone by the first line of b8. Silence again in b8. From l17 in b9 a light, dry plucked figure (the series' caper motif, slowed) enters very quietly and builds a little under the key and the register in b10. It stops dead on the second knock in the pre-lap. b11 has no music; the door shut and the hold play on silence. Instrumental, no melody line over dialogue, no percussion hits.
ending_question: The people of Imlipur trusted a fake uniform and were turned away by the real one, so how can she get even one complainant to put a thumb in the register before the microphones go up at ten?
writer_notes: English adaptation (S5) of script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Same top-level, character, beat and line keys as the Hindi file and as content/proof/photoreal/script.en.json; same beat ids (b1 to b11), line ids (l01 to l27), speakers, order, on_screen, silences and emotion tags. Only text, target_seconds, the character names, voice_notes, title, language fields, the quoted line in the b6 sfx note and the quoted 'Sudhir Nirala.' in the b1 action differ. action, locations, sfx_notes, music_note and ending_question are otherwise copied unchanged: picture, effects and music are shared between the two cuts.

Register: Nandini is clipped, educated Indian English; Nirala is manual English with no contractions ('kindly', 'the same', 'It was already stamped by SHO sahab, madam?'); Pushpa is plain and short; Ramsevak is one tired plain sentence. Kept as Indians say them in English: madam, thana, FIR, SHO sahab, ji, almirah, Bhaiyaji. Nobody calls Nirala 'Inspector'. No bare 'sahab': always 'SHO sahab'.

One word per object, matching the Hindi choices: 'stamp' for मोहर (l09, l14, l15, l16), 'signature' / 'signed' for sign (l09, l13), 'papers' for काग़ज़ (l08, l10, l18), 'sacks' for बोरी and for माल (l09, l11, l17), 'lock' for ताला, 'key' for चाबी, 'register' for the FIR register, 'the accused' for मुलज़िम in the dictated tag (l04) and 'prisoner' in Pushpa's line (l06), where the Hindi uses मुलज़िम in both; Pushpa would not speak in seizure-memo English.

Choices that are not word for word: l03 'Only... kindly let the cap stay.' (बस... cap रहने दीजिए). l06 'Even the lock had forgotten how to open.' keeps the joke on the lock and, like 'भूल गया था', says it has been forgotten for a long time (critic rerun). l13 'Gone. At ten past twelve. On SHO sahab's signature.' follows the rerun Hindi 'गया। बारह दस पर। SHO साहब के sign पर।' and uses the same 'ten past twelve' as l11 so the time is heard twice in one form. l11 needs no change for the rerun's 'minute' to 'मिनट' fix: the English says 'Ten past twelve'. l25 'So this is zero crime.' already has the rerun Hindi's word order; only its target moves. l07 adds 'o'clock' so a lone 'Twelve' is not misheard as a fragment. l11 'Ten past twelve' (as the logline says) rather than 'twelve ten'. l14 says outright what 'मोहर पहले से SHO साहब की थी' implies: it was already stamped. l16 'invitation' for बुलावा, as the bible's timeline calls the midnight call. l19 'At ten this morning', because it is past midnight (the bible's note against 'कल'). l20 'kept in front of them' is Indian English for placed. l22 drops 'kindly' to stay inside the Hindi line's 1.8 s; Nirala already says 'kindly' three times (l03, l05, l18). l26 says 'your FIR' so the line is about Ramsevak's own complaint. l27 'We went to the real thana once, madam.': 'once' carries 'once was enough', the plain past is flatter and more final than 'have already been', and it does not answer the ending question.

Length (hand count, no tool: this session has no shell). English dialogue is about 1,180 characters (1,153 before the critic rerun; +7 on l06, +20 on l13) by the D-016 direction 7 method (code points with spaces and punctuation, no tags, no space after a tag). That is above the 1,050 figure, but that measure was set for Devanagari Hinglish, where a syllable takes fewer code points than in Latin-script English; what binds the English cut is duration against the Hindi, which is below. Count error likely a few characters either way.

Timing, estimated by ear, not measured: 27 lines, spoken targets 100.9 s (about 11.7 characters a second, slower than the proof English targets of 13 to 15, because Gate 0b showed v4 overrunning those), plus 14 speaker changes at 0.3 s (4.2 s), plus 18.1 s of silence: target_total_seconds 123.2, against 127.6 for the Hindi (critic rerun: l06 5.6 to 5.8 s, l13 2.6 to 4.3 s, l25 1.8 to 2.0 s, b3 silence 3.0 to 2.0 s; was 122.1). Every line is within 15% of its Hindi target; the changed lines are l06 -6%, l13 +5%, l25 -5%. b6 now plays l09 alone over the slip insert (5.4 s) and l10 alone over her face (2.0 s); b9 is one line per shot for l17 to l20 (4.2, 6.4, 4.6, 4.2 s) and l21 with l22 on the two-shot (5.3 s with the speaker gap), so no English shot runs past 8 s. Longest relative to Hindi: l17 (4.2 against 3.8, +11%), l10 and l12 (2.0 against 1.8, +11%), l19 (4.6 against 4.3, +7%). Shortest: l27 (3.8 against 4.4, -14%), l24 (4.2 against 4.8, -13%), l15 and l21 (3.2 against 3.6, -11%). The shots follow the measured voice (D-014 rule 6, D-0M2), so short English lines are not padded; if a held shot feels thin, the hold carries it.

Gate 0b risk: v4 takes ran 20 to 60 per cent over target. Twenty per cent over on speech would put this cut at about 143 s. If it measures over 135, use the Hindi script's cut order: shorten silences (b3, b4, b11); then l25; then l05; then fold l23 into l24 ('The second key, madam. Two years I've waited for someone to ask.' as one line, about 0.5 s saved). Protected lines are the same as in the Hindi: l01, l06 to l11, l16, l18 to l22, l26, l27.

Tags are the Hindi tags, in the same positions. [calm], [quietly], [sharply], [nervous] and [sighs] were used in the proof scenes. [hesitant] (l03, l21), [deadpan] (l06, l23), [flatly] (l11, l16, l25) and [earnest] (l18, l22) are in the verify group and not yet confirmed for any Series 2 English voice; S10's swaps are the same as for the Hindi ([hesitant] to [quietly], [deadpan] or [flatly] to [calm], [earnest] to [calm]). Nothing is whispered. [sharply] on l08: full voice, clipped, a command across a running engine; not shouted (matches the rerun Hindi note). It is Glimpse A's last line and has to project over the diesel idle. No ellipsis follows a tag directly.

Short-turn flags for the voice director: l02 'Yes, madam.' (11 characters) cannot be merged (D-016 direction 11, so Glimpse A starts on l03 as a whole line); record extra takes. l22, l23 and l25 are 21 to 22 characters and carry 'madam' or 'So' as a stabilising word.

Glimpse A in English is the same lines: l03, b4 shot 3 with l06 if it fits, l07, then l08, ending on 'Stop. Show me the papers.'. By these targets: 2.6 + 5.8 + 3.6 + 2.0 s of speech plus holds. If the cut runs over, drop l06 first. Cut before b6's paper rustle, which belongs to shot 2.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Imlipur (IM-lee-poor), Nirala (ni-RAA-laa), Sudhir (su-DHEER), Bhaiyaji (BHAI-yaa-jee), Tripathi (tri-PAA-thee), Ramsevak (raam-SAY-vuk), thana (THAA-naa), sahab (SAA-hub), ji (jee), almirah (ul-MEE-raa), SHO and FIR spelt out as letters.
